The Mars Sample Return Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agencys website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO High & Medium Gain Antenna Pointing Assembly (HGA & MGA APA) unit it in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

APA shall provide the capability to move and point two antenna types: a ca. 2m parabolic reflector for HGA and a 90° offset steerable 20 cm reflector for MGA. The APA is intended as the moving mechanisms plus the relevant electronics.
APA requirements:
-	Dual Axis APM in azimuth and elevation axis arrangement
-	Pointing capability of Azimuth: -180° + 180°, Elevation: 0° -90°
-	Max slew rate: ≥0,5°/s
-	Max Acceleration ≥ 0,01°/s2
-	Pointing accuracy: better than 0.05° for HGA and 0.1° for MGA
-	Position sensing in each axis (resolution 0.008°)
